title: Decision: Role and Identity separation in Caller struct
description: Why this is good: The Caller struct separates role (the authorization outcome: Owner or Peer) from identity (the verified claim: user_id, login_name, display_name). This prevents a subtle class of bugs where a handler might check role without remembering to check if the identity is valid, or vice versa. By making both fields required and distinct, the type system ensures they're kept in sync. A handler that receives Caller can trust both fields unconditionally — they've been verified together by the extractor. This is better than passing them separately (where one could be forgotten) or mixing them in an identity-with-embedded-role struct (which is awkward to pattern match).
